learningObjectives.title: Food production (microorganisms, fish farming and glasshouses)

questions.q: Which microorganism is used in the production of both bread and beer?
questions.explain: Yeast is a fungus used in baking and brewing because of its ability to respire the sugars present.

questions.q: When yeast respires anaerobically, glucose is converted into which two products?
questions.explain: Anaerobic respiration (fermentation) in yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Why does bread dough rise during baking?
options: Carbon dioxide from yeast respiration is trapped in the dough
Ethanol produced by yeast evaporates from the dough
Oxygen is released by the flour
Lactic acid makes the dough expand
questions.explain: The carbon dioxide gas made by respiring yeast is held in the dough, forming bubbles that make it rise.

questions.q: Yoghurt is produced from milk using which type of microorganism?
questions.explain: Lactobacillus bacteria ferment the sugar in milk to convert it into yoghurt.

questions.q: In yoghurt production, the bacteria convert the lactose in milk into which substance that thickens and sours it?
questions.explain: The bacteria produce lactic acid, which lowers the pH and causes the milk proteins to thicken.

questions.q: The antibiotic penicillin is produced in industrial fermenters by which organism?
questions.explain: Penicillin is made by growing the mould (fungus) Penicillium in a fermenter.

questions.q: Why must aseptic conditions be maintained inside an industrial fermenter?
options: To prevent contamination by unwanted microorganisms
To increase the temperature of the fermenter
questions.explain: Aseptic precautions stop competing microorganisms entering and spoiling the culture or product.

questions.q: On a fish farm, young fish are often kept separately and graded by size. What is the main reason for this?
options: To reduce predation of smaller fish by larger fish
questions.explain: Separating fish by size limits intraspecific predation, so more fish survive to be harvested.

questions.q: Growers sometimes add extra carbon dioxide to the air in a glasshouse. How does this increase crop yield?
options: It increases the rate of photosynthesis
It increases the rate of respiration
It reduces water loss from the leaves
It kills pests on the plants
questions.explain: Extra carbon dioxide raises the rate of photosynthesis, so the plants grow faster and produce a greater yield.

questions.q: Which statement best describes selective breeding?
options: Choosing organisms with desired characteristics to breed together
Changing an organism's genes using enzymes
Producing genetically identical copies of an organism
questions.explain: Selective breeding means humans choose the parents with useful features and breed them together.

questions.q: Why must selective breeding usually be carried out over many generations?
options: The desired feature becomes more pronounced with each generation of selection
The characteristic appears fully developed in the first generation
It allows new genes to be created by mutation each time
Clones are produced in every generation
questions.explain: Repeated selection of the best individuals gradually enhances the desired characteristic over generations.

questions.q: What is one disadvantage of repeatedly selectively breeding from a small number of individuals?
options: Reduced genetic variation in the population
Increased genetic variation in the population
An increase in the natural mutation rate
The immediate formation of a new species
questions.explain: Selective breeding reduces genetic variation, which can make a population more vulnerable to disease.

questions.q: A dairy farmer wants a herd of cows that produce more milk. What should the farmer do over several generations?
options: Breed together the cows and bulls from the highest milk-yielding stock
Feed all the cows a larger quantity of food each day
Keep the cows in a warmer glasshouse environment
Insert a milk gene into the cows using a plasmid
questions.explain: Choosing the highest-yielding animals as parents each generation gradually raises the milk yield of the herd.

questions.q: In genetic engineering, what is the small circular loop of DNA taken from a bacterium and used as a vector called?
questions.explain: Plasmids are small rings of bacterial DNA into which a useful gene can be inserted.

questions.q: Which type of enzyme is used to cut a required gene out of a length of DNA?
questions.explain: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific points to isolate the desired gene.

questions.q: The human insulin gene is inserted into a bacterial plasmid. Why are the modified bacteria then grown in large numbers?
options: So that they multiply and produce human insulin
So that they turn into human cells
So that they produce animal insulin instead
So that they destroy the inserted insulin gene
questions.explain: Each bacterium carries the insulin gene, so growing many of them produces large quantities of human insulin.

questions.q: A crop plant is genetically modified to carry a gene giving resistance to insect pests. What is a likely advantage of this to the farmer?
options: Higher crop yield with reduced use of insecticide
The crop no longer needs any water
The crop grows without any sunlight
The crop reproduces only by cloning
questions.explain: Insect resistance means fewer plants are damaged and less insecticide is needed, raising the yield.

questions.q: Plants produced by micropropagation (tissue culture) are best described as being:
options: Genetically identical to each other and to the parent
Produced by the fertilisation of gametes
questions.explain: Micropropagation produces clones, so the new plants share identical genes with the parent.

questions.q: Micropropagation produces genetically identical plants because the cells divide by which process?
questions.explain: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells, so the cloned plants have the same genes as the parent.

questions.q: To clone a mammal by nucleus transfer, the nucleus taken from a body cell of the animal is placed into which cell?
options: An egg cell that has had its own nucleus removed
A fertilised egg containing two nuclei
questions.explain: The body-cell nucleus is inserted into an enucleated egg cell, which then develops into a clone of the donor animal.
